newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada arrests Saudi, may be linked to Saudi attack.
newsitem.headline: Canada arrests Saudi, may be linked to Saudi attack.

text.p: Canada's security agency said on Saturday immigration officials had arrested a Saudi man and a Canadian paper reported that he was a suspect in the bombing in Saudi Arabia last year that killed 19 U.S. soldiers.
The FBI said it wanted to question the man arrested on Tuesday in Ottawa about the massive truck bomb attack on an apartment complex housing U.S. troops in Dhahran last June.
The FBI identified the man as Hani Abdel Rahim Hussein Al-Sayegh, 28.
A spokesman for Canada's security service said Al-Sayegh was arrested under a warrant signed by the solicitor general and the immigration minister.
Gaetan Blais, an officer at the Canadian Security Intelligence Service (CSIS), told Reuters he could give no further details on the case until a closed-door court hearing.
"The case will be heard in an in camera hearing, probably within a week. Then, depending on what the judge decides, he may face a deportation hearing," Blais said.
The Toronto Sun, quoting unnamed government officials, said Sayegh had been arrested on suspicion of being "engaged in terrorism" and being a threat to "the security of Canada."

The paper also quoted unnamed sources as saying Sayegh was picked up at an Ottawa grocery store after a tipoff that he was a suspect in the bombing that ripped through an apartment complex in Dharan last June.
He has been in Canada since last August, when he applied for refugee status, and has been under CSIS surveillance since November, the newspaper quoted insiders as saying.
In Washington, the Federal Bureau of Investigation said it hoped to question the man about the Dhahran bombing.

An FBI statement said the U.S. agency was grateful for "the vigilant actions of Canada" and praised the government of Saudi Arabia for its "invaluable assistance leading to the identification and location of Al-Sayegh."

Al-Sayegh is the second alleged suspect in the Dhahran bombing to be arrested in Canada. On Dec. 6 last year, Fahad Shehri, 21, was arrested in Ottawa on allegations he told authorities he belonged to a group connected to the bombing.

However, he has said he was not involved and on March 16, Saudi Arabia's deputy interior minister was quoted by a London-based Saudi-owned newspaper as saying Shehri was not being sought in connection with the blast or any other crime.
The explosion last year that killed 19 U.S. servicemen and wounded scores of others came less than a month after Saudi Arabia beheaded four anti-U.S. Moslem militants.
The militants had been convicted of an earlier bombing in Riyadh in November 1995 in which five Americans and one Indian were killed.
